//: Profile TEMPLATE for a third (Linux) machine — copy to e.g. linux.json,
fill in the placeholders, and drop the '.example' suffix. Pair with the
systemd units documented in README.md (#systemd-unit) and
docs/machine-setup.md (periodic sync timer) rather than the launchd
templates (docs/launchd/), which are macOS-only.
Fill in:
<linux-hostname>   short, stable name for this machine, e.g. 'thinkpad'
— used for the 'profile' field and stateDir path
below (both local-only); it must NOT be used for
repositorySubdir, see the warning below.
<linux-username>   the OS user agent-memory-sync runs as
<repo-path>        absolute path to this machine's checkout of the
agent-memory-sync-adjacent workspace, matching
whatever Claude Code encoded into its memory slug
(see the namespace-divergence note in macbook.json
/ mac-mini.json — every machine's slug embeds its
own absolute path and OS username, so copy the
slug straight out of `ls ~/.claude/projects/` on
THIS machine rather than guessing it).
repositorySubdir is intentionally the fixed literal 'pandora' below, NOT
a <linux-hostname>-style placeholder — do not customize it per machine.
It is the ONLY thing that determines the remote tree path (see
toRepositoryRelativePath in src/memory-sync/config.ts) and MUST be
identical across every machine sharing this remote; giving each machine
its own repositorySubdir (which this template used to do, mirroring the
'profile' field) makes every machine write to a separate top-level tree
in the same bare repo and none of them ever see each other's pushes — a
live cross-machine E2E test caught exactly this on macbook.json/
mac-mini.json before it was fixed. The 'profile' field IS meant to be
customized per machine (<linux-hostname>) — it never touches the
remote. It also has NO effect on any file path in this template
specifically: resolveRunConfig() only derives stateDir from 'profile'
(.agent-memory-sync/<profile>) when stateDir is NOT set explicitly,
and stateDir IS set explicitly below — so 'profile' here only ends up
recorded as a cosmetic label inside this machine's state.json. Fill it
in anyway, for a self-documenting invocation and a correct label.
syncPaths' FIRST entry is a directory entry covering the ENTIRE rootDir
(source '.'), so every file agent-memory-sync finds there is synced,
including future subdirectories, without listing individual
files/folders by name. destination is the non-'.' literal 'memory', not
'.': a bare '.' destination round-trips through push but is silently
unmappable on pull/restore (mapRemotePathToLocalAbsolute's
directory-prefix match needs a real path segment, not '.'). The walk
skips hidden files/dot-directories (.DS_Store, ._* AppleDouble shadows,
'.git', ...) and never follows symlinks under rootDir — both by design,
see isHiddenEntryName in src/memory-sync/config.ts and
src/memory-sync/git-client.ts.
syncPaths' SECOND entry is machine-state (absolute source
/home/<linux-username>/.harness/machine-state, destination
'machine-state'), carrying this machine's toolchain snapshot for the
cross-machine parity check run by the harness companion 'session-start
toolchain-parity'; see docs/machine-setup.md section e) for the full
payload convention (one file per machine, owner-writes-only) and
section f) for the THIRD entry, frictions. Both entries set
"ownerScoped": true, matching the real linux.json/macbook.json/
mac-mini.json profiles, so push only ever offers this machine's own
<profile>.json under machine-state/ or frictions/ and never a peer's
file this machine merely pulled; see collectLocalSyncFiles'
ownerFilter option in src/memory-sync/config.ts.
stateDir is set OUTSIDE rootDir (a separate ~/.agent-memory-sync tree),
which matters now that syncPaths covers the whole rootDir: if stateDir
stayed nested inside rootDir, the recursive walk would also pick up
this tool's own internal git working copies/queue/base snapshots and
try to sync them as if they were memory content. An absolute stateDir
value overrides the rootDir-relative default entirely — see
resolveRunConfig() in src/config/loader.ts.
rootDir/stateDir use a resolved absolute path, not '~': agent-memory-sync's
config loader does not perform shell-style tilde expansion — see
src/config/loader.ts resolveRunConfig().
Activation: pass BOTH --config (this file) and the profile name
positionally, e.g.:
agent-memory-sync run <linux-hostname> --config profiles/linux.json
The CLI's [profile] positional argument always defaults to 'default'
and overrides this file's 'profile' field when omitted. Since stateDir
is set explicitly below, that override has no effect on where state
files land here specifically — pass the positional argument anyway
for a self-documenting invocation and a correct 'profile' label.
